title: Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy, a preseason Heisman hopeful, will not return this season: Source
content:
Ole Miss star running back Kewan Lacy will not return to the field this season, a source close to the program confirmed. The source spoke on condition of anonymity because the school had not made an official announcement on Lacy’s status. On3 first reported that Lacy was done for the year.

Lacy entered the season as a Heisman Trophy candidate and was set to team up with quarterback Trinidad Chambliss as of the most dangerous quarterback-running back duos in college football. Ole Miss launched a joint Heisman campaign in August by placing Lacy and Chambliss on the massive LED display on the exterior of Sphere in Las Vegas. Lacy injured his left shoulder during the Rebels’ marquee win over LSU in mid-September but missed only one game, a loss at Florida, before returning to the field. He reaggravated the injury in the Rebels’ 34-27 loss to Texas on Oct. 24 and has not played since.

In August, The Athletic’s Dane Brugler had Lacy rated as the top running back in the 2027 NFL Draft class and under consideration as a potential first-round pick, but Lacy was absent from Brugler’s updated top-50 rankings this week. He has played three seasons of college football and so will have the option to put off the draft for another year.

After spending his first year of college at Missouri, Lacy arrived at Ole Miss ahead of the 2025 season and was prolific for the Rebels under former Ole Miss coach Lane Kiffin and offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. His 104.5 rushing yards per game in 2025 were good for ninth nationally and second in the SEC, only behind Missouri’s Ahmad Hardy. He and Chambliss took the Rebels to the College Football Playoff semifinals last season, handling Tulane in Oxford and knocking off SEC champion Georgia in the Sugar Bowl before losing thriller to Miami in the Fiesta Bowl.

When Kiffin left the program for LSU and took many key players and coaches with him, Lacy and Chambliss both stayed to play under Pete Golding.

Without Lacy, a steep climb back to Playoff contention gets more daunting for the Rebels. After a 42-7 home loss against Georgia on Saturday, they fell from No. 10 in the CFP rankings to No. 19. Things have not fully come together for the Rebels since what looked like a signature win against Kiffin and LSU in Week 3. They followed that emotional victory up by losing by 24 in Gainesville, and the Bulldogs’ 35-point win was the worst loss of Golding’s nascent head coaching career. The Rebels’ CFP odds would rise to 51 percent in Austin Mock’s projections if they beat Oklahoma this weekend before season-ending home games against Wofford and Mississippi State, but they will need some help from above them in the rankings to make the field.

If this is the end of Lacy’s Ole Miss career, he’ll finish with 1,955 rushing yards and 29 touchdowns across two seasons with the Rebels. He set single-season program records last year for rush attempts with 306, rushing yards with 1,567 and rushing touchdowns with 24.

In his place, Ole Miss has turned to junior running back Makhi Frazier. Through eight games, Frazier has 72 carries for 365 yards. His best game of the season came against Missouri on Oct. 17, when he rushed for 101 yards in a 31-3 win.

Lacy looked poised for a huge 2026 after an outstanding sophomore season in which he forced nearly 90 missed tackles. The 5-foot-10, 205-pounder runs with explosion and balance through the smoke, but he has not really been a home-run hitter. Injuries have hurt his stock this season, but other backs simply have been better.

Florida’s Jadan Baugh is the complete package; Utah’s Wayshawn Parker, who joined Dane Brugler’s top-50 board this week, has been a walking big play; Missouri backup-turned-starter Jamal Roberts has been tremendous in place of Ahmad Hardy (who might be the most talented back on the board, if he gets back to 100 percent). Lacy would be wise to spend another year in college. — Nick Baumgardner
